entries.subject: DAMIT 9541: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-9541.txt. Model 9541, version 2022-11-29, pole (168°, 56°), period 231.2 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Physical scale
entries.finding: The retained calibration uses 6.586 ±0.128 km. The thermal effective spherical diameter is used as an approximate volume-equivalent display scale; no joint shape/thermal inversion or independently measured volume is implied.,Quoted ±0.128 km is the catalog fit error; approximately 10% additional systematic diameter uncertainty applies.,Slow spin can leave the thermal observations sensitive to viewing aspect and incomplete rotation coverage; the diameter is an approximate global display scale.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: The Shape lens uses cssEarth's existing shared grid to identify unavailable imagery.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Other DAMIT matches
entries.finding: [Other DAMIT matches](https://damit.cuni.cz/?q=2440) — Inspected for calibrated replacements; retain the selected solution and disclose available alternatives. The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 9542: pole (353°, 55°), 231.3 h, version 2022-11-29. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A model-specific comparison establishes whether an archived alternative improves the selected shape or resolves its pole/scale ambiguity.
